speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help us understand what's going on, can you describe the specific movements you've been experiencing and when you first noticed them? Also, are you currently taking any new psychiatric medications or supplements?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any feelings of inner restlessness or an inability to sit still that you feel compelled to move to relieve? Have you noticed any involuntary muscle stiffness, tremors, or facial grimacing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. To rule out other causes, have you experienced any tremors, muscle stiffness, or changes in your heart rate or blood pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your symptoms and recent medication history, I am confident in the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced akathisia
